name: roof-above-wired2
notes: The wired roof machine, armed on BOTH clock edges (one armed window every 6 ticks). Roof slab y 3..5 bedrock, target T [0,5,0]. Machine: A [0,6,0] piston facing west; X [1,7,0] stone; O [1,8,0] observer facing up; Ro [1,9,0] repeater delay 1 facing east (input from [2,9,0]) on top of O: O watches it. Updater 1: U [0,6,3] sticky facing north, block K starting at [0,6,2], powered through Ru [0,6,4] repeater delay 2 facing south. Updater 2: U2 [3,6,0] sticky facing west, block K2 starting at [2,6,0], powered through Ru2 [4,6,0] repeater delay 2 facing east. Crawl ceiling slab [0,7,-1]. Clock: R1 [8,6,0] repeater delay 3 facing west, R2 [8,6,2] delay 3 facing east, loop dust [7,6,0..2] (S, R2's output) and [9,6,0..2] (S' = NOT S, R1's output), started by one pulse of the observer [10,6,1] facing east (place a block at [11,6,1]). S runs west along z=2 ([6..3,6,2]), climbs a staircase to Ro (dust [2,7,2] on block [2,6,2], [2,8,1] on [2,7,1], [2,9,0] on [2,8,0]) and branches south then west to Ru ([3,6,3..5], [2..0,6,5]). S' runs from [9,6,-1] along z=-2 ([9..5,6,-2]) to Ru2 ([5,6,-1], [5,6,0]). Each clock edge: Ro flips 2 ticks later, O fires 2 ticks after that; on S's falling edge Ru falls in that same tick (U pulls K away from A), on S's rising edge S' falls and Ru2 falls in that tick (U2 pulls K2 away from A): either way A is updated while O powers it, extends, O switches off silently, and A's head landing arms it.
